Thus, all thirty-six *kulanāyikās* (leaders of the families) come into being: six having the form of the tastes (*rasa*), six having the form of the elements (*dhātu*), six having the form of the sense-faculties (*indriya*), six having the form of the objects of the senses (*viṣaya*), six having the form of the organs of action (*karmendriya*), and six having the form of the objects of the organs of action. Likewise, there are six that set in motion form, six that set in motion feeling (*vedanā*), six that set in motion perception (*saṃjñā*), six that set in motion mental formations (*saṃskāra*), and six that set in motion consciousness (*vijñāna*), as well as six that set in motion gnosis (*jñāna*). Thus, the thirty-six *kulanāḍīs* (channels of the families) should be known to become seventy-two through the relationship of support and supported.
Thus it is said: "The channels of the Kālacakra are twice [in number] at the uṣṇīṣa," meaning they take the form of four petals; these four flow during the four junctions (saṃdhyā).

At the heart, there are eight channels, beginning with Rohiṇī, which serve as the support for the samāna and other winds, flowing according to the eight days of the week through the division of the watches (prahara) each day.
Here, below and above the two channels, the wind is to be placed; thus,
there are sixteen "kings" (nṛpati) in the head that set the lunar days (tithi) in motion,
and the number of teeth (thirty-two) in the throat— meaning twenty-eight constellations (nakṣatra) in the throat-cakra, plus thirty-two that set the four danda-constellations in motion.

At the navel, in the navel-lotus, outside the *rāśi-nāḍīs*, are the *ghaṭī-nāḍīs*: sixty-four *nāḍīs* (eight multiplied by eight), which carry the sixty mandalas, flow as the four voids, and set the sixty-four *daṇḍas* in motion;
these are the "twice the kings," meaning thirty-two *nāḍīs* in the center of the secret [lotus], which carry the thirty-two constituents beginning with semen.

The six channels (nāḍīs) that obstruct the wheels, which seize the ten sense objects and possess the nature of the humors' combination (sannipāta), are doubled again and again; multiplied further, they are the portions of phlegm, bile, and wind.

These indeed are the "death-channels" (mṛtyu-nāḍīs) [by day], yet by the power of the Guru’s injunction, they bestow longevity and health. In the six wheels, these very same wind-channels remove the fear of death for yogis; there is no wonder in this. || 58 ||

Among these, six channels are the obstructors of the six wheels (*cakras*); ten are the carriers of the sense objects, and they are of the nature of *sannipāta*. These are doubled again as portions of phlegm (*śleṣman*), making twenty; doubled further as portions of bile (*pitta*), they become forty; and again as portions of wind (*anila*), they become eighty. Thus, one hundred and fifty-six channels established in the six wheels are to be understood as the channels of the Kālacakra.
Indeed, these are the channels of death, yet by the power of the Guru's instructions, they bestow longevity and health.

In the six cakras, the channels of time (kālanāḍīs) are said to remove the fear of death when cultivated through the guru’s instruction; that this is so for yogins is no wonder. In the uṣṇīṣa are four [channels], in the forehead forty-eight, which are the disturbances of the phlegm constituent (śleṣmadhātu); in the throat thirty-two, in the heart-lotus forty-eight, which are the disturbances of the bile constituent (pittadhātu); in the navel sixty-four, and likewise in the secret place sixteen, which are the disturbances of the wind constituent (vāyudhātu). In the secret place, another group of six is manifest as the fixed obstructions of the combined humors (sannipāta). || 59 ||

At the *uṣṇīṣa*, there are four channels, as in "the oceans and the four" (*abdhiścatasraḥ*); at the forehead, there are sixteen, as in "the oceans multiplied by the yugas" (*jaladhihatayugāḥ*). These twenty channels cause the provocation of the phlegm element (*śleṣmadhātu*). At the throat, there are thirty-two channels, as in "the teeth" (*dantāḥ*). In the heart-lotus, there are eight channels, as in "the eyes multiplied by the yugas" (*nayanahatayugāḥ*). These forty channels cause the provocation of the bile element (*pittadhātu*). And at the navel and the secret place, respectively, there are sixty-four channels, as in "the oceans and sixty" (*abdhiṣaṣṭiḥ*).
The king [of channels] is also in the secret lotus; externally, in the middle perimeter, there are sixteen channels—these eighty channels are the outbursts of the wind element.
In the secret [lotus], there are ten other channels beginning with the east, and six others in the middle perimeter, and [six] in the inner perimeter, according to their respective numbers.

The *sannipātas* (conjunctions) and the aggravations of the *sannipātas*... [text fragment] ...thus, the one hundred and fifty-six channels of the *Kālacakra* are established in the nature of male and female deities. When cultivated together with the channels of the six families, these channels—which bestow death upon the ignorant—bestow happiness upon yogins. The *Kālacakra* consists of one hundred and sixty-two channels, which are the essence of the channels of the six wheels (*ṣaṭcakra*).

Furthermore, among those one hundred and sixty-two channels (*nāḍī*), each individual channel is of ten types by way of the movement of the ten winds and the nature of the ten aggregates (*skandha*) and elements (*dhātu*).
Thus, all of them multiplied by ten become sixteen hundred and twenty in number, flowing as the *ghaṭikā*s of the twenty-seven lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*).
In this way, O Glorious One, in the Paramādibuddha of the Mandala of Lunar Mansions, there are this many deities by way of wisdom (*prajñā*) and means (*upāya*).

Therefore, from this extensive circle of constellations, according to worldly convention, the goddesses who carry the elements such as phlegm (*śleṣman*)—extracted by Mañjuśrī for the sake of accomplishing mundane siddhis or for the sake of accomplishing the perfection of the body—are the "leaders of the six wheels. This is the rule regarding the intermingling of the channels (*nāḍī*) of Kālacakra.

Now, the protection of the channels of the six families is stated, beginning with the word "six": "The six channels block the wheels; they proceed along the three paths through the divisions of moon, sun, and fire. They must be protected within the body by the power of the guru’s injunctions, for they are those which bring death to living beings."

If the entry of the vital breaths into the six occurs for men, then indeed there is the destruction of death; for when [the breath] has not entered the subtle [channel], the domain of immortality is severed by yogis.

In this body, those six channels which are said to obstruct the wheels (*cakras*), which proceed along three paths—namely, the paths of the moon, sun, and Rāhu, corresponding to the left, right, and middle paths, and the upward, downward, feces, urine, and semen paths according to the division of moon, sun, and fire—must be guarded by the yogi within the body. Why? Because of the constraint of the Guru.

The "constraint of the Guru" is the yoga of six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅgayoga*); by means of that, these six [channels] which bring death to living beings must be guarded from death, for it is through them that the vital breath (*prāṇa*) enters.

If the entry of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) occurs at all times within the six [channels] for human beings, then death is indeed destroyed. Among these six, the subtle *avadhūtī* is the central channel (*madhyamā*). When the vital breath has not entered that subtle [channel], the domain of death is cut off by yogis; however, it is not the case that the domain of death is not cut off.

Thus, in the *Vimalaprabhā*, the twelve-thousand-verse commentary on the *Laghukālacakra-tantrarāja* following the *Mūlatantra*, this is the fourth great chapter (*mahoddeśa*): "The Internal Wheel-turning King and Mleccha War; the Arising of the Family of Channels in the *Kālacakra*-Family Tantra. Now, the signs of untimely death for embodied beings are explained, beginning with the words "If the vital breath" (*prāṇa*), etc.: "If the vital breath flows through a single channel day and night, life lasts for one year. If it flows uninterruptedly through one side [of the body] for one fortnight, the life of humans lasts for one and a half years."
The third [chapter]. || 3 ||

[Chapter on] the Great Instruction on the Characteristics of Untimely Death and the Severing of the Channels: "O Lord of Men, when [the breath] flows for one uninterrupted month, life lasts exactly three months; thus, O Kālacakra, the yogi knows death as the movement of the moon within his own body. (61)

In this body, the navel-cakra is a twelve-spoked wheel of the zodiac signs (*rāśicakra*), consisting of alternating odd signs beginning with Aries (*meṣa*) and even signs beginning with Taurus (*vṛṣabha*). Consequently, the movement of the vital breath (*prāṇasañcāra*) occurs in the left nostril during the six odd signs beginning with Aries.
In the ascendants beginning with Taurus (Vṛṣabha), the movement of the vital breath occurs in the right nostril.
There are twelve transitions (saṃkrāntis) every day, occurring at intervals of five *daṇḍas* each.

Thus, by means of sixty *daṇḍas* in a full day and night, there are twelve transitions: six in the left nostril, six in the right nostril, and [six] in the central channel (*madhyamā*) during the twelve entries.

The equilibrium of the elements (*dhātu-samatva*) exists in those bodies free from disease, whereas for those overcome by disease, there is a disharmony (*vaiṣamya*) among the *vāta*, *pitta*, and *śleṣman* elements. From this disharmony arises the disharmony of the vital breath (*prāṇa*).
Consequently, if the breath flows for a full day and night through a single channel—the left—then life lasts for a full lifespan.

The lifespan of humans is characterized by a full hundred years as the medium duration. If it flows without interruption for one fortnight, then the life span becomes slightly more than a year; after that, one goes to death. If it flows continuously and without interval in the left channel for one month, then the life span becomes three months.
Thus, in his own body, the yogi knows the movement of the moon and death according to the *Kālacakra*.

Regarding this matter of fatal signs (*ariṣṭa*), the *Kālacakra* is the twelve-spoked wheel of the zodiac signs; having drawn that very wheel upon the ground, one should place the days of the fatal sign and the thirty-six months of life on the first petal.

Then, for one month it does not flow [through the left channel], and there is an increase in the days of the fatal sign. At the end of the second month, upon entering the third month, it flows for two days through the left channel on that very same petal.
Then, during the third month, [the breath] does not flow; at the end of the fourth month, upon entering the fifth month, the vital breath flows through the left channel for three days.
Then, from the fifth month, it does not flow during the sixth month.
Thus, over six months, there are three days of ill omen (*ariṣṭa*): three days in the middle, and at the end, the right and left [channels] possess the nature of ill omen.
*Ariṣṭa* is untimely death; *riṣṭa* is death within the limit of one hundred years. Thus, from thirty-six months plus the days of *ariṣṭa*, six months of life have passed.
Thereafter, there is no movement of the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) on that leaf [of the life-span].
By means of eleven transits, a day and night passes with twenty-one thousand six hundred inhalations and exhalations.
In this regard, there is no deficiency in the cycle of breaths even when the leaf of the zodiacal sign is abandoned.
Therefore, on the second leaf, it flows for four days, five days, and six days respectively in the seventh, eighth, and ninth months.
Then, another three months of the thirty-month lifespan have passed.
Thereafter, having taken twenty-seven months, the vital breath (*prāṇa*) circulates in the third leaf and abandons two leaves.
It completes a day and night through ten transits (*saṃkrānti*), as the vital breath moves across ten leaves.
From among the twenty-seven months, in each month again, the left channel flows for seven days, eight days, or nine days.
Consequently, another three months become deficient from the twenty-seven months.
In this manner, according to the previously stated method, it discards the third zodiacal sign.
The vital breath (prāṇa) performs its transition through the nine petals;
thus it flows through the left channel for ten days, eleven days, or twelve days,
and thereafter it abandons the fourth petal.
Then, after twenty-four months, the life span becomes deficient by three months.
Likewise, it is deficient by thirteen days, fourteen days, or fifteen days; the word "then" (*tataḥ*) is not present [in some versions].
In the *Vimalaprabhā*, [it says]: "Then he discards the fifth petal."
It effects the transition through seven petals;
for twenty-one months, it becomes three months less, and thus it flows through sixteen days, seventeen days, and eighteen days respectively in each month.
Then, it abandons the sixth petal.
It effects the transition through the six petals;
thus, from eighteen months, three months are subtracted from the lifespan.
In this manner, it flows for nineteen days, twenty days, and twenty-one days.
Then, within a single day and night, the vital breath (*prāṇa*) abandons the seventh petal and performs a transition into five petals.
Consequently, from fifteen months, the lifespan becomes diminished by three months.

Likewise, when it flows for twenty-two days, twenty-three days, or twenty-four days, it then abandons the eighth petal and performs transitions into four petals; consequently, from twelve months, the lifespan becomes diminished by three months.

When it flows for twenty-five days, twenty-six days, and twenty-seven days, then it abandons the ninth petal and performs a transition through three petals; thus, of the life-span, three months are subtracted from nine months.

Likewise, when it flows for twenty-eight days, twenty-nine days, and thirty days, then it abandons the tenth petal and performs a transition through two petals; thus, of the life-span, three months are subtracted from six months.

Likewise, when [the breath] flows for thirty-one days, thirty-two days, or thirty-three days, it then abandons the eleventh petal and transfers its transition to one petal; thus, from three months, ninety days are subtracted from the lifespan.
Thereafter, it flows for three days on the previous petal and for two days on the twelfth petal.
Then it abandons the twelfth petal, and finally flows for one day in the pericarp (karṇikā) until the cessation of the breaths of the life-force wheel occurs.

"Then, by means of the fatal sign (*ariṣṭa*) in the left channel, those men who are not practitioners of yoga go to their death. This is the rule regarding the lunar fatal signs in the left channel. Due to the divisions of *sattva*, *rajas*, and *tamas*, the number of fatal days increases by one each month.

Herein is the arrangement of the zodiacal wheel (*rāśicakra*): having made the zodiacal wheel double-layered, the fatal days are placed in the first layer, and in the other layer, the remaining months of life corresponding to those fatal days are placed.
Here, on the first spoke of the wheel, there are three days of misfortune and thirty months; on the second enclosure, there are six days of misfortune and twenty-six remaining months of life.

Thus, in the third spoke, there are nine days of misfortune (*ariṣṭa*) and twenty-four months; likewise, in the fourth, twelve days and twenty-one months; in the fifth, fifteen days and eighteen months; in the sixth, eighteen days and fifteen months; in the seventh, twenty-one days and twelve months; in the eighth, twenty-four days and nine months; in the ninth, twenty-seven days and six months; in the tenth, thirty days and three months; and in the eleventh spoke of the wheel, there are thirty-three days of misfortune.
At the end, there is the depletion of the three months.

Prior to that, for three days not yet ascended, [the breath] flows on the first petal of the wheel in the right channel (*dakṣiṇanāḍī*) for the purpose of depleting the constituents (*dhātu*) of the right channel; for two days it flows on the twelfth petal;
and for one day it flows in the central channel (*madhyamā*), the *avadhūtī*, for the purpose of depleting the wheel of breaths.
Therefore, the departure of the vital breath occurs through the left channel during the lunar omen; such is the rule regarding the lunar omen.

Now, the fatal signs of the Sun (*sūryāriṣṭa*) in the right channel are described starting with the words "from five," and so forth: From five, the movement of twenty-five days ascends by an increase of five; from that, by an increase of one, it reaches the ten multiplied by three (thirty), up to thirty-three. At the time of the constellation Puṣya, all those months—numbering eighteen (three eyes, moon, six, and three times four)—are the remaining days of life, which are fifteen hundred and twenty-two (tithis, directions, arrows, qualities, and two moons). [End of] the Great Chapter on the Signs of Death through the Cessation of the Channels in the Section on Fatal Signs.

In this body, the Moon, having taken up the qualities of the Sun—sattva, rajas, and tamas—shows the days of death (ariṣṭa); the Sun, having taken up the qualities of the Moon—sound, touch, form, taste, and smell—shows the days of death.

[The process proceeds] by five and then five more until reaching the fifth house (pañcarāśi); then two houses by one [day] each; then, starting from the base, it ascends for thirty-three days: it leaves the eighth house in fifteen days, the ninth house in ten days, the tenth house in five days, and the eleventh house in three days.
In this manner, the vital breath ascends through the right channel for thirty-three days.

Then, within the twelve zodiac signs, it remains for two days in the left channel for the purpose of depleting the constituents (*dhātu*) of the left channel, and for one day in the central channel for the purpose of depleting the wheel of breaths (*śvāsacakra*). After that, death occurs.
For example, from the fifth limit-day until the twenty-fifth day, the movement of the day ascends by increments of five.
In the five zodiac signs [beginning from Aries], there are fifteen, fifteen, twenty, and twenty-five days for each birth.

Therefore, by increasing by one day in succession, there are thirty-six and thirty-seven days respectively in the sixth and seventh signs for the purpose of exhausting the *sattva* and *rajas* qualities.
Then, when the time of *Pauṣṇa* arrives, the vital breath (*prāṇa*) ascends through three tens—that is, thirty days—in the eighth, ninth, and tenth signs.

Then, in the eleventh [year], there is the month plus three days until the end. The total number of years and remaining days of misfortune (*ariṣṭa*) within the zodiacal wheel, starting from the birth sign among the twelve signs, is as follows: for the Moon in the third eye [the Sun]—that is, in the birth sign, there are three years; in the second sign, two years; and in the third, one year. Thus, these are the total years and remaining days of misfortune for life. Then, regarding "six, three, four, and moon" (*ṣaṭ-tri-yug-mendavaḥ*): in the fourth sign, there are six months; in the fifth, three months; in the sixth, two months; and in the seventh, one month of remaining days of misfortune for life.

From that place of birth, the seventh position is the *pauṣṇa* [sign], Capricorn (*makara*), which is the month of conception for those born from a womb. From that, the seventh is the month of the birth of the vital breath (*prāṇa*), Cancer (*karkaṭa*), due to the increase and subsequent abandonment of the lunar *nāḍīs*. At the end of the twelve zodiac signs, it becomes Capricorn again; thus, thirteen months pass from conception. Therefore, Cancer is the birthplace of the vital breath (*prāṇa*), and not of the sun alone.
Then it rises.
From that birth, when the sign of Capricorn (makara) has risen as the seventh zodiacal sign, the setting of the sun is called the time of Pauṣṇa.
From that time onward, the vital breath (prāṇa) becomes irreversible; it cannot be stabilized within the body by gods, asuras, or humans.

"The time of moonrise during the portion of the night" means that "moonrise" refers to the entry of death into the white element (*śukradhātu*). It is not the rising of the white element itself, but rather the entry of the fatal wind (*ariṣṭavāyu*).
Then, from the time of the *pauṣṇa* [period], for the purpose of the waning of the semen (*śukra*), the vital breath (*prāṇa*) ascends through the right channel for thirty-three days;
thereafter, for two days in the left channel, and for one day in the middle channel.

The remaining days are: fifteen from the lunar dates (*tithi*), ten from the directions (*diś*), five from the arrows (*iṣu*), three from the qualities (*guṇa*), and two from the number two; thus, there is one day of life—this is the rule for the single explanation of the solar fatal sign (*sūryāriṣṭa*).
Now the second explanation is stated, beginning with "from its own place" (*svasthānāt*) and so forth:

From its own place, the wheel of zodiac signs (*rāśicakra*) is abandoned by the remaining portions of the supreme digits (*parakalā*), through years, months, and days equal to [the number] three-eyed, moon, six, three, yoke, and moon;

and from the asterism of Pūṣan (*pauṣṇa*), there is indeed a loss through [the number] lunar days, directions, and qualities (*guṇa*). When these have entered the pericarp (*kaṇikā*), at the end of the day marked by the three, death occurs through the conjunction of the Sun and the enemy (*ariṣṭa*).
In this body, within the lotus of the navel, there is a wheel of zodiac signs (*rāśicakra*) consisting of twelve channels (*nāḍī*).

Therein, the place of birth is the first channel of the zodiac sign; whatever *lagna* (ascendant) belongs to the child at the time of its conception in the womb, that very sign—Taurus and so forth—is of the nature of the *samanā* channel.

From that own-place, the wheel of zodiac signs, which is a wheel of channels with twelve spokes and consisting of sixty mandalas, is abandoned by the supreme digit (*parakalā*), the power of breath (*prāṇaśakti*).

Regarding the phrase "by the equal remainders of the decrease": the decrease consists of the days of ascent—five, ten, fifteen, twenty-five, twenty-six, and twenty-seven. The remainders of the decrease are three years, two years, one year, six months, three months, two months, and one month. By these remainders of the decrease, starting from the first leaf up to the seventh *nāḍī*-leaf, the sequence proceeds by means of years and months: with three eyes and moons (three years), it abandons three *nāḍīs*; with six, three, pairs, and moon (six months), it abandons seven *nāḍīs*.

And by days equal to the limit of the Pauṣṇa [period], from the point of birth, the time of the sun's setting is the seventh; this is the period of *rajas*. Therefore, from that Pauṣṇa [point], by days of ascent and life-span equal [to those], there is the abandonment of the zodiacal *nāḍīs* of the vital power (*prāṇaśakti*). [Specifically]: a lunar day (*tithi*) in fifteen days, a direction (*dik*) in ten days, an arrow (*iṣu*) in five days, and a quality (*guṇa*) in three days. By these thirty-three days, one abandons through the solar flow via the single right channel the eighth, ninth, tenth, and eleventh *nāḍīs*—the zodiacal *nāḍīs* that carry the five mandalas.
For twelve days in the left channel (*vāmanāḍī*), and for one day in the middle channel (*madhyamā*), he enters the pericarp (*kaṇikā*).
Thus, by thirty-six days from the beginning of summer, death occurs for men through the conjunction with the ill omen (*ariṣṭa*) of the Sun; this is the rule for the second explanation.

Previously, he abandons the world of the five arrows and three fires—that is, the number of days of three solar years—and from that point, in the third [year], he [traverses] forty-five, forty-two, and thirty-nine [days].

The eyes (2), snakes (8), mountains (7), and arrows (5) constitute one [set]; another [set] consists of Vasus (8), hands (2), and seven; and from that, Rohaṇa (6) [is added]. Thus, all [the values] beginning with the lunar days (tithi) and the total number of days extend as far as the pericarp (kaṇikā).
In this zodiacal wheel, the nāḍī of the birth ascendant is called "prior";

in that leaf of the birth ascendant, from among the total number of days amounting to one thousand and eighty, one discards a period of thirty-three days and thirty-five [additional] days—namely, thirty-five days plus thirty-three days—after three years.

Then, having emptied that leaf, the vital power (*prāṇaśakti*) enters the second leaf, taking with it the remaining number of days. From that total of days, she abandons on the second leaf a remainder consisting of three hundred and forty-five days—calculated as "arrows, pairs, and peacocks" (546)—along with ten days for ascending from the previous leaf to the subsequent one.
Then, taking what remains, she enters the third leaf, and the second leaf becomes empty.
Again, right there on the third leaf, she abandons one hundred and seventy days, along with fifteen days for ascending, leaving the third leaf.
Having taken the remainder, it enters the fourth [petal]; the third becomes empty.
Then, together with twenty days beginning from the ascent and so forth—namely, the "two minus the eyes" (82)—it abandons eighty-two days in the fourth petal;
having taken the remainder, it enters, and the fourth becomes empty.
Furthermore, together with twenty-five days of ascent, [the breath] abandons fifty-seven days at the fifth petal;
having taken up the remainder, it enters the sixth, and the fifth becomes empty.
Again, together with twenty-six days of ascent, it abandons twenty-eight days at the sixth petal.
Then it enters the seventh petal, and the sixth becomes empty.
Then, having abandoned the group of twenty-seven days of ascent in the seventh,
it takes the remaining group of thirty-six days and enters the eighth petal, and the seventh becomes empty.
Then, on the eighth [day], it abandons fifteen days;
having taken the remaining twenty-one days, it enters the ninth, and the eighth becomes empty.
Then, on the ninth, it abandons ten days.
Taking the remainder of eleven days, it enters the tenth; the ninth becomes empty.
Then, from the tenth, it abandons five days;
taking the remainder of six days, it enters the eleventh; the tenth becomes empty.
Therein, he abandons three days;
taking the remaining three days, he enters the twelfth, while the eleventh becomes empty.
Therein, he abandons two days.
Taking one remaining day, it enters the pericarp (*kaṇikā*), and the twelfth petal of the zodiacal channels becomes empty.
Thus, by means of the one thousand and eighty intermediate days of the sun over three years, the vital energy (*prāṇaśakti*) abandons the twelve-spoked wheel of the zodiac.
Thereafter, for one day, the central channel (*madhyamā*) flows within the pericarp.

Then, having abandoned the wheel of breath (*śvāsacakra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*) effects a transition elsewhere through the six destinations (*ṣaḍgati*) along with the vital air (*prāṇavāyu*); such is the rule regarding the omens of death (*ariṣṭa*) for the Sun.

Herein is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): as in the previous *nyāsa*, according to the distinction of years and the distinction of days to be abandoned, there is the placement of the days of the omens of death in the first enclosure and the placement of the remaining days of life in the second enclosure.

In the second wheel (*cakra*), there is the placement (*nyāsa*) for the abandonment of days; on the eastern petals, there is the sequential placement of *śūnya*. This is the rule for solar misfortune (*sūryāriṣṭa*): for those born at an even ascendant (*samalagna*) in the right channel (*dakṣiṇanāḍī*) of the Sun, and for those born at an odd ascendant (*viṣamalagna*) with little lifespan due to lunar misfortune (*candrāriṣṭa*). Thus ends the rule for solar misfortune.

Now, the intermediate signs of death (*madhyamāriṣṭa*) according to the sequence of years—which were taught by the ignorant followers of non-Buddhist schools (*tīrthika*) and which cause delusion among beings regarding the limit of a hundred-year lifespan—are here refuted. In this regard, it is said by those non-Buddhist schools: "If there is a flow of five *nāḍīs* in the right channel, the lifespan is one hundred years; with a flow of six *nāḍīs*, the lifespan is ninety years; with a flow of seven *nāḍīs*, the lifespan is eighty years; with a flow of eight *nāḍīs*, the lifespan is fifty years; with a flow of nine *nāḍīs*, the lifespan is thirty-three years; with a flow of ten *nāḍīs*, the lifespan is twenty-six years; with a flow of fifteen *nāḍīs*, the lifespan is fourteen years; with a flow of thirty *nāḍīs*, the lifespan is twelve years; with a flow for one day and night, the lifespan is ten years; with a flow for two days, the lifespan is eight years; with a flow for three days, the lifespan is six years; and with a flow for four days, the lifespan is five years."
Thus, according to the flow of five days, the lifespan is three years; this is the rule for the nadīs and breaths of the heretics (*tīrthika*) on the right path.
That very [rule] does not hold when examined through reasoning and the words of the Omniscient One.
Here, in the case of humans where no fatal signs (*ariṣṭa*) are present, the vital wind flows for five *daṇḍas* in the left and right channels during the five even and odd *lagnas*.

For a person with a lifespan of one hundred years, the increase of breath occurs for seven years on the left and right [nostrils] according to the distinction of the solar transits (*ayana*); thereafter, for sixty years, there is an increase of *pāṇīpala*s according to the distinction of the increase of the transits; thereafter, for thirty years, there is an increase of *nāḍī*s according to the distinction of three-month periods; and thereafter, for three years and three fortnights, there is an increase according to the distinction of days—this is the principle of the increase of time.

According to this principle, for one who suffers premature death—such as death occurring three years, five years, twelve years, or twenty years after conception—the flow of six or seven *nāḍīs* beyond the five *nāḍīs* is useless, because the limit for death following conception is three years.

In this regard, if the death of the newborn occurs after a month has passed, then starting from the day of birth, the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*) ascends from the time of the constellation Puṣya by the measure of lunar days, directions, arrows, and qualities (154).

Thus, at the end of two months, three months, four months, six months, one year, two years, or three years from conception, death occurs by reversing the ascent of thirty-three days down to the ascent of five days in the right channel through the destruction of the five qualities, sound and so forth; and in the left channel, it occurs through the destruction of the three qualities, sattva and so forth, over the course of one day.

Thus, death is to be known from the first day after conception due to the entry of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) into the *kaṇikā* (pericarp); likewise, death occurs on the third day due to the arising of the vital breath in the twelfth petal; similarly, on the sixth day, due to the arising of the vital breath in the eleventh petal; likewise, on the eleventh day, due to the arising of the vital breath in the tenth zodiacal petal; similarly, on the twenty-first day, due to the arising of the vital breath in the ninth zodiacal petal; and thus, on the thirty-sixth day, due to the sequential arising of the vital breath in the eighth zodiacal petal.

Thus, in two months, the arising of the breath (*prāṇodaya*) occurs at the seventh zodiacal leaf; likewise, in three months, it occurs at the sixth leaf due to the arising of the breath; likewise, in four months, it occurs at the fifth due to the arising of the breath; likewise, in six months, it occurs at the fourth leaf after twenty days due to the arising of the breath; likewise, in one year and a half, it occurs at the third due to the arising of the breath; in two years, it occurs at the second after ten days due to the arising of the breath; in the third year, it occurs at the first due to the arising of the breath; and in the fourth year, there is no rule regarding the days, from the time of conception up until the end of one hundred years—this is the rule for the solar fatal signs (*sūryāriṣṭa*).

Just as with the Sun, so too, due to the distinction between the three qualities (guṇas) such as *sattva* and so forth, there is a fixed rule for the lunar portents (*candrāriṣṭa*) from the time of conception; likewise, it was stated by Īśvara in the *Kālottara*, in the section on the upward flow (*ūrdhvaśrotra*): "As is the left [channel], so is the non-left [right], and likewise the middle;
at the end of three years, she eats the sacrifice.
Thus, even in the *Parasiddhānta*, there exists a certain fixed rule; this is the fixed rule for the lunar and solar portents.

Thus, from the first day up until the end of three years, whatever death of a child occurs—whether by way of the lunar path or the solar path—it is divided into one thousand and eighty distinct types according to the specific daily variations of death. There is no fixed rule here for those born from a womb regarding their karma;
rather, the count of the vital breaths (*prāṇa*) is known through the days of ill omen (*ariṣṭa*) by means of the flow of breaths in the channels (*nāḍī*).
Therefore, the wheel of ill omens and the wheel of death consist of the sequential abandonment of the five-maṇḍala flow of the vital breath from the channels of the zodiacal signs.
Then, the principle is that entry into the *kaṇikā* (the central point) signifies death on that very day.

This characteristic of the three-year period—wherein the death of all sentient beings is said by the Blessed One to occur through the flow of the *madhyamā* [channel] as conceived for the limit of a hundred years—is indeed [explained];
however, by means of the moon’s three-fortnightly law, there would be no fatal sign (*ariṣṭa*) of death for the moon itself.

In this context, that by which death as an ill omen (*ariṣṭamaraṇa*) does not occur for the moon has been conceptualized by the ignorant who lack awakening. For example, it is the statement of the ignorant that "there is no death as an ill omen in the left channel due to the nature of the moon, whereas death as an ill omen is taught by the Omniscient One to occur in the right [channel] due to the flow of the sun," because here the presiding deity of the three years is referred to by the word "sun."
The *prāṇa* wind is designated by the word "moon" (*candra*), while the *apāna* wind is the lord of the three fortnights (*tripakṣādhipati*).

The *prāṇa* is the sun and the presiding lord of the *iḍā*, *piṅgalā*, and *suṣumnā*; it flows upward from the navel. The *apāna* is the lord of the channels of feces, urine, and the moon; it flows downward from the navel. This is the great section concerning the severance of the channels characterized by the signs of death and misfortune (*ariṣṭa*). Thus, below the moon are the three qualities (*guṇatraya*), and above the sun are the five qualities corresponding to the objects of the five spheres (*pañcamaṇḍala*).

By that threefold division, there is the omen of the Moon (candrāriṣṭa) on the left, and by the fivefold division, the omen of the Sun (sūryāriṣṭa) on the right; this is the rule for the omens of the Moon and Sun in the downward and upward channels. Now, the characteristic of death at the full time of the central channel is described, beginning with "the year of time" (kālābda): "As long as one [digit] ascends by the power of the daily movement, transitioning through the path of the Sun known as the Moon, increasing by one alternately on odd and even days in sequence."
Furthermore, the distinction of the transits on the uneven and even days in the twelve-spoked wheel causes [the life span] to be exactly one and a half months, while the life itself is thirty nights.

In this body of men and women, the flow of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) proceeds through the left and right channels by means of the five maṇḍalas for ninety-six years plus ten and a half months, according to the divisions of *sattva*, *rajas*, and *tamas*.
For humans with a lifespan of one hundred years, the period of the central channel lasts for three years and three fortnights; such is the rule.

In that regard, there are three channels—the left, the right, and the middle—which have the nature of *sattva*, *rajas*, and *tamas* respectively; among these, Death, having assumed the count of the flow of the *tamas* channel, [acts] by means of the nature of *prāṇa* and *apāna*.

On the left and the right, during odd and even days, one ascends for a period of three years and three fortnights—this constitutes the year of time (*kālābda*)—according to the movement of the days. These days number one thousand one hundred and twenty-five; by virtue of their movement, one ascends and transmigrates until the exhaustion of the lifespan. On the left path called "Moon" (*candrākhye vāmamārge*) and on the right path of the Sun, one ascends by an increment of one day through odd and even days respectively. If birth occurred in an odd zodiacal sign such as Aries, one ascends one day in the left channel (*vāmanāḍyāṃ*); if birth occurred in an even sign such as Taurus, one ascends two days in the right [channel].

Then, furthermore, he performs the division of transits by means of unequal and equal days at the conclusion of the ascent through the left and at the conclusion of the ascent through the right, according to the measure of the days of ascent.

Thus, in the twelve-spoked wheel of zodiac signs, he performs the transit sequentially for the relinquishment of the five mandalas: in the left channel, he performs the transit for the purpose of exhausting the mandalas beginning with space, and in the right channel, he performs it for the purpose of exhausting the mandalas beginning with earth.

Here, on the left side, by ascending five days, the vital wind (*prāṇa-vāyu*) abandons the flow of the void element (*śūnyamaṇḍala*) during the six transition days in the six odd signs beginning with Aries; on the right side, by ascending six days, the *prāṇa* abandons the flow of the earth element (*pṛthivīmaṇḍala*) during the six transition days in the six even signs beginning with Taurus. Thus, in the left channel, it abandons the air element (*vāyumaṇḍala*) in eleven days, and in the right petals, it abandons the water element (*udakamaṇḍala*) in twelve days.
Thus, in seventeen days, he abandons the fire-maṇḍala in the left petals; in eighteen days, he abandons the fire-maṇḍala in the right petals;
again, in twenty-three days, he abandons the water-maṇḍala in the left petals; in twenty-four days, he abandons the wind-maṇḍala in the right petals;
and once more, in nineteen days, he abandons the earth-maṇḍala in the six left petals.
"In thirty days on the right, it abandons the sphere of space;

likewise, by ascending through the left and right channels on alternating and even days, there is the abandonment of the five spheres in the twelve channel-petals of the zodiacal signs over thirty days—that is, thirty days of transits.
Then, by ascending for thirty-one days in the left channel, there is the depletion of the *sattva* element in the odd petals."
By ascending thirty-two days through the right channel over thirty-one days of transits, the element of *rajas* (passion) is exhausted;

likewise, by ascending thirty-three days over thirty-two days of transits, the element of *tamas* (darkness) is exhausted in the odd petals, over thirty-three days of transits. Thus, the exhaustion of the phlegm-channel occurs through the ascent of the breath.
In the *Vimalaprabhā*, it is stated that the element of passion (*rajo-dhātu*) is the depletion of the bile channels, and the element of darkness (*tamo-dhātu*) is the depletion of the wind channels;
this occurs through the ascent of thirty-three days, meaning by means of thirty-three days of transits.

When the days of the transits of both zodiac signs are totaled, there are one thousand one hundred and twenty-two days, less the three days of three years and three fortnights; thus, there is the severing of the channels of the elements of passion, darkness, and sattva within the five mandalas.
The abandonment of the location of the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) occurs thus: for one and a half months—that is, for three hundred and sixty days—by means of the ascent of the vital breath;

thereafter, for another thirty days, which constitute the number of days in the month of conception, [this lasts] until the end of the three nights of life. During these thirty-three days, there is an ascent through the right channel (*dakṣiṇanāḍī*), an absence of all solar transits (*saṃkrānti*), and the disintegration of the aggregates (*skandha*) and elements (*dhātu*).

In this context, the thirty-three days constitute the cessation—the absence of mutual conjunction—of the five aggregates beginning with form (*rūpa*), the five elements beginning with earth (*pṛthivī*), the five sense organs beginning with the body organ (*kāyendriya*), the five objects beginning with smell (*gandha*), the five action organs beginning with the anus (*guda*), and the five objects of the action organs beginning with speech (*ālāpa*). Following that, for one day, [the breath] enters the *madhyamā* channel in order to exhaust the wheel of breaths (*śvāsacakra*).

The sixth aggregate (*skandha*), the sixth element (*dhātu*), the sixth faculty (*indriya*), the sixth object (*viṣaya*), the sixth organ of action (*karmendriya*), and the object of the sixth organ of action—the emission of semen occurs at the end of death; such is the rule for the cessation of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases. Now, the ascent of the breaths of the dying, as described in the *Jātakas*, is explained beginning with the words "the breaths" (*śvāsān*): "The breaths, the smeared [digits], the channels, and the periods of day and night ascend by way of transition; through seven years, the limbs of the solstice, and by virtue of the movement of the solstice, they ascend through sixty years."

Due to the movement of the sun, thirty years and three months, along with the fortnights and years of time, become thirty-two and a half days; from the Kālacakra, this constitutes the period of ascent.

In this body, there is the breath-wheel (*śvāsacakra*), the *liptā*-wheel, the *ghaṭikā*-wheel, and the day-wheel (*dinacakra*); as they exist externally, so too do they exist within the body. Therein, the breath-wheel consists of six breaths; the *pāṇīpala*-wheel consists of sixty *pāṇīpalas*; the *ghaṭikā*-wheel consists of sixty *ghaṭikās*; the wheel of misfortune (*ariṣṭacakra*) consists of one thousand and eighty days; and the wheel of the days of time-death (*kālamṛtyudinacakra*) consists of one thousand one hundred and fifty-six days.

In these wheels, death ascends through the left channel and the right channel respectively, in the form of breaths, in the nature of *pāṇīpala*, in the nature of *ghaṭikā*, and in the nature of days, increasing by one at each stage;
first, it ascends as breaths for seven years, and then [it ascends] by the signs of the solstices (*ayana*). Thus it is said.

For one born here who has no untimely death (ariṣṭa) within the limit of a hundred years, the life-force wind (prāṇavāyu), which carries the five elements (pañcamaṇḍala), flows through both channels—the left and the right. Then, in the third year, during the fifth transit (ayana), it ascends by one breath into the space-element (ākāśamaṇḍala) in the left channel; in the sixth transit, it does not ascend. Then, in the seventh transit, during the fifth transit of the third year, it ascends by two breaths into the earth-element (pṛthivīmaṇḍala) in the right channel; in the eighth transit, it does not ascend. Thus, in the seventh [year], there is an ascent into the void (kha).

Regarding "trayomāna" in manuscripts *ka* and *kha*, it refers to three years and so forth. Furthermore, in this chapter, within the section on the Great Summary of the Signs of Death and the Cessation of the Channels (*ariṣṭamaraṇalakṣaṇanāḍīcchedamahoddeśa*), the breath ascends three times through the left channel in the space mandala, but not in the eighth [month].
Thus, on the ninth day, four breaths ascend in the earth-maṇḍala of the right channel;
on the tenth, or again on the eleventh, five breaths ascend in the void-maṇḍala of the left channel;
on the twelfth, and then on the thirteenth, six breaths ascend in the earth-maṇḍala of the right channel during that solstice; and on the fourteenth solstice...

Thus, six breaths constitute one *cakra*, which is a *liptā* or a *pāṇīpala*. Here, [this amounts to] seven years minus half a month; therefore, after the *liptā-cakras*, there is no further ascent of breaths. By the nature of the *liptās*, the *liptās* ascend by means of sixty years due to the movement of the solstice (*ayanagati*).

Then, from the age of seven years onwards until the sixtieth year, during the alternate solstices, he ascends by one day and so forth through unequal *pāṇīpala*s up to fifty-nine *liptā*s in the left channel (*vāmanāḍī*) within the space-maṇḍala; and in the right channel (*dakṣiṇanāḍī*) within the earth-maṇḍala, by the second day and so forth, through equal sixty *pāṇīpala*s across every six petals, which possess the natures of odd and even *lagnas*. This wheel of *pāṇīpala*s, consisting of sixty *pāṇīpala*s, constitutes a single *ghaṭikā*.

Therefore, up to the limit of sixty-seven years, the channel ascends by way of the nature of the death-channel; thus, starting from thirty years and three months, beginning with one channel, it ascends through the left and right channels alternately via the odd and even channels. During the first half of the solstice, it ascends one channel in the left channel within the space-mandala over three months;
during the other three months, and again during the second half of the solstice over three months, it ascends two channels in the right channel within the earth-mandala.

Thus, in three months, one ascends through sixty *nāḍīs* in the six zodiacal petals on the left and right—on the space-maṇḍala and the earth-maṇḍala—by way of the nature of the *nāḍīs* of death. Therefore, up until the limit of ninety-seven years minus half a month, one ascends the wheel of *nāḍīs*. That itself becomes one day; then, by way of the nature of the day, one ascends the wheel of days in the left and right *nāḍīs* according to the previously mentioned sequence. Thus, by virtue of the movement of the days, [death ascends] by means of years of time, fortnights, and triple years.

From the word "ca" (and), it is understood that [the calculation] is by three fortnights and three additional days. Here, the number of days for the ascent from the *kālacakra* is derived from eleven hundred and twenty-five—divided by thirty-two and a half—and this resulting sum of days is to be known as extending up to the *kaṇikā*.

Among these, the days obtained for the ascent by means of the division of thirty-two and a half are thirty-four; the *ghaṭikās* are thirty-six; the *pāṇīpalas* are fifty-five; and there are two and a half breaths (*śvāsa*). Among these, one day remaining at the *kaṇikā* should be understood as the left and right *ariṣṭa* (fatal signs).

The daily ascent increases by one *ghaṭikā*, and the final ascent occurs in the right channel; such is the rule for the death by time. Now, the severing of the channels of the navel-center and so forth is described, beginning with the words "in each fortnight" (*pakṣe*): In every fortnight, nine times eight channels (seventy-two) are severed in the navel center; at each joint, the Fire-day (the Sun) abandons one channel. In the action-wheel called the throat, he abandons the lunar channels day by day. Within a month, he gradually abandons the lunar stations located in the *bindu*; within a fortnight, the Lord of the Moon (the Moon) abandons the weekday-channels situated in the heart.

Here, at the navel, there are sixty channels of the twelve zodiac signs that carry the sixty mandalas. "Eight serpents multiplied by nine" means eighty-one; when multiplied by nine, they become seventy-two. Therefore, in the navel-cakra where the serpents are multiplied by nine, one channel is severed in each fortnight (*pakṣa*). Here, a fortnight is to be understood as eighteen days. By that fortnight, the channel carrying the mandala beginning with Space flows in the left.
Then: Who carries *ka* and *kha*?
In the *Vimalaprabhā*, it is stated that one abandons thirty channels over three years; on the right side, one abandons thirty channels that carry the mandalas beginning with Earth.

Thus, by means of thirty-three fortnights, sixty [channels] are abandoned by the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) throughout all the mandala-channels, having abandoned a sixth part. By means of the fortnights of the three years, one abandons the channel that carries the five mandalas.
It flows through and abandons each individual channel in fifteen days within the "action-wheel" (karmacakra) known as "activity" (kriyā).

Here, in this body, the action-wheel consists of twelve wheels divided into twelve parts, corresponding to the twelve months; it is located in the six joints of the two hands and the six joints of the two feet.

In each joint-wheel there are thirty channels; thus, in the twelve joints, there are three hundred and sixty channels. Among these, in the joint of the right shoulder and arm during the month of Makara, there are thirty channels according to the division of the thirty lunar days (*tithi*); in the joint of the left shoulder and arm during Phālguna, there are thirty channels according to the division of the thirty lunar days. Likewise, in the joint of the right forearm there are the channels of Caitra; in the joint of the left forearm, the channels of Vaiśākha; in the joint of the right wrist, the channels of Jyeṣṭha; and in the joint of the left wrist, there are thirty channels according to the division of the thirty lunar days of Āṣāḍha.

In the two hands, at the wheel of action (*karmacakra*), there are one hundred and eighty channels in the six types [of joints]. From there, in the joints of the right thigh and hip, there are thirty channels according to the lunar days (*tithi*) of the month of Śrāvaṇa; in the joint of the left thigh and hip, there are thirty channels of Bhādrapada. Likewise, in the joint of the right knee and thigh, there are thirty channels of Āśvina; in the joint of the left knee and thigh, there are thirty channels of Kārttika; in the joint of the right ankle and knee, there are thirty channels of Mārgaśīrṣa; and in the joint of the left ankle and knee, there are thirty channels by way of the nature of the lunar days of the month of Puṣya.

Thus, in the two feet, there are one hundred and eighty channels in the six joints of the *karmacakra*; since the *karmacakra* is that which brings about the activity of the organs of action (*karmendriya*), [the breath] ascends through these channels by means of three days at a time for each of the "peak days" (*śikhidina*).

With these three thousand eight hundred days of the three-year period, the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*) abandons three hundred and sixty *nāḍīs* in that which is called "Action" (*kriyā*). It is called "Action" because it performs actions such as grasping and moving. In the sixty joints of the fingers and toes of the hands and feet, there is a wheel (*cakra*) consisting of six *nāḍīs*. This wheel, whose nature consists of the *nāḍīs* of earth, water, fire, air, space, and gnosis, is situated in each joint and consists of six *nāḍīs*.
In the sixty joints of the limbs, there are three hundred and sixty channels (*nāḍī*); he abandons each individual channel every three days, just as in the wheel of karma.
When he abandons thirty channels at the joint of the right forearm, he then abandons six channels in each of the five fingers of the right hand;
thus, he abandons thirty channels in the five fingers over the days of a month, which are the lunar dates (*tithi*).
In this same way, it should be understood for the left side:
when he abandons the joints of the right upper arm and forearm, he then abandons thirty channels in the joints of the middle phalanges of the fingers;
the same applies to the left side as well.
When he abandons [the breath] at the joint of the shoulder and upper arm, then he abandons thirty channels in the joints of the lower phalanges of the fingers over thirty days;
thus it should be understood for the left side as well.
When he abandons thirty channels at the joint of the right knee, then he abandons thirty channels in the joints of the half-phalanges of the right toes over thirty days.
Likewise, when [the breath] abandons the joint of the right knee on the left side as well, it then abandons thirty channels in the middle joints of the fingers;
this should be understood to apply similarly to the left foot.
When [the breath] abandons the joint of the right hip and thigh, it then abandons thirty channels (*nāḍī*) in the joints of the phalanges below the toes;
this should be understood to apply likewise on the left side.

Now, the presiding letters of the channels are stated: here, the *ka*-group, differentiated by the short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*) in reverse order, resides in the joint of the left shoulder and arm.

Thus, at the joint of the right shoulder and upper arm is the *ka*-group, differentiated by the long vowels beginning with *jñāna* (e, ai, o, au, am, aḥ); at the joint of the left upper arm and forearm is the *ca*-group, differentiated by the short vowels beginning with *ākāśa* (a, i, u, ṛ, lṛ, m). At the joint of the right hand and forearm is the *ṭa*-group, differentiated by the six long vowels beginning with *jñāna*; likewise at the left, it is differentiated by the six vowels beginning with *ākāśa*.
Thus, for six months, [the letters] *kha*...
On the left, Ka Kha.

In the northern course (*uttarāyaṇa*), there is the severance of the channels (*nāḍīccheda*) characterized by the signs of imminent death (*ariṣṭamaraṇa*) through the long measures (*mahāmātrā*) beginning with *jña*;

therefore, at the joint of the right hip and thigh, there is the class of *pa* (*pavarga*) distinguished by the long measures of knowledge (*jñāna*) and so forth. On the left side, there is the class of *ka* (*kādivarga*) distinguished by the short measures (*hrasvamātrā*) beginning with space (*ākāśa*).

Thus, at the joint of the right knee, there is the *tavarga* (the dental class), which is non-different from the six long vowels beginning with *jñāna*; on the left, it is non-different from the six short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*).

Likewise, at the joint of the right foot and knee, there is the *savarga* (the palatal class), which is non-different from the six long vowels beginning with *jñāna*; on the left, it is non-different from the six short vowels beginning with space, starting with the consonants of space in reverse order.
In this way, each class consists of thirty syllables through the division of long and short vowels within the twelve wheels of the *karmacakra*, which has thirty spokes.

Then, within the wheels of action (*kriyā-cakra*), each consonant beginning with *ka* is distinct from the six long vowels beginning with *jñāna* (ā, ī, ū, ṛ, lṛ, ai). In each of the joints of the right hand, beginning with the thumb—specifically at the joint below the thumb, which consists of six channels—the consonant *ka* is distinct from the vowels beginning with *jñāna*. At the joint of the index finger is *kha*; at the joint of the middle finger is *ga*; at the joint of the ring finger is *gha*; and at the joint of the little finger is *ṅa*, each being distinct from the six long vowels beginning with *jñāna*.

At the joint below the little finger of the left hand is the letter *ṅa*, distinguished by the six short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*); at the joint of the ring finger is *gha*; at the joint of the middle finger is *ga*; at the joint of the index finger is *kha*; and at the joint of the thumb is *ka*, distinguished by the six short vowels beginning with space. Thus, on the second row of joints of the right hand, starting from the thumb, is the *ca*-group (*cavarga*) distinguished by the long vowels; on the left, it is distinguished by the short vowels. Likewise, on the third row of joints of the right hand is the *ṭa*-group (*ṭavarga*) distinguished by the long vowels; on the left, it is distinguished by the short vowels.

Thus, in the first year, on the joints of the right toes, the *pa*-group is differentiated by long vowels; on the left, it is differentiated by short vowels. On the middle joints of the right hand, the *ta*-group is differentiated by long vowels; on the left, it is differentiated by short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*). On the upper joints of the right hand, the *sa*-group is differentiated by long vowels; on the joints of the left fingers, it is differentiated by the six vowels beginning with space in reverse order. In the second year, they are differentiated by the *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* substitutions; in the third year, the six groups are differentiated by the *yaṇādeśa* and other such rules.
The detailed explanation of this will be stated in what follows, so it is not elaborated upon here:
"Day by day, within a month, he gradually abandons the channels of the lunar mansions in the throat.
This means that in the throat-cakra, there are channels for the twenty-eight lunar mansions; he abandons them over twenty-eight days consisting of vowels.

The lunar station (*śaśipada*) situated at the *bindu* and located in the forehead, consisting of fourteen channels, is abandoned in the middle of a fortnight over fourteen days by means of the fourteen *pluta* vowels.

The channel of the [lunar] day (*vāranāḍī*), consisting of eight [channels], is abandoned in eight days by means of the qualities such as the objects and the *sattva*. The thirty consonant-natured channels situated in the secret place are abandoned; this is the rule for the severance of the channels regarding death by time (*kālamaraṇa*).

Now, regarding the cutting off of the forward and reverse movement of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) within the wheels of action through its solar nature, the [movement] of the channels is described by means of the designations of the *vargas* (groups), beginning with the words "from the *vargas*" and so forth: The Sun moves from the *vargas* together with their vowels according to the divisions of the zodiac signs for the duration of a solstice (*ayana*). Thereafter, day by day, he moves in reverse order, increasing by one [sign] each day, until the year of time is exhausted.

When the year is cut off, within the middle of the fortnight, by virtue of the days of the vowels, there is ascent and descent; and at the time of day and night, there is the loss of inhalation and exhalation, which constitutes a single night of life. (68)

In the *Vimalaprabhā*, regarding the internal [system]: here, in the wheel of karma (*karmacakra*) consisting of twelve spokes, there are wheels composed of thirty channels (*nāḍī*) at each of the twelve joints of the hands and feet. Within those twelve wheels, which are presided over by the thirty lunar days beginning with the month of Māgha, the six groups of consonants beginning with *ka*—distinguished by the six long vowels starting with the visarga—are situated in the six joints of the right hand and feet according to the order of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), by way of the phonetic properties (*vyañjanadharma*) of earth and so forth, as well as the phonetic properties of space and so forth, according to the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*). Furthermore, according to the recitation of *pratyāhāra* beginning with *ṅa*, the six groups of consonants, distinguished by the short vowels of space and so forth, are situated in the six joint-wheels of the left hand and feet.

The sun moves through those classes along with their vowels together with the vital breath (prāṇavāyu) and death, [completing] a solstice (ayana) by means of the divisions of the zodiac signs. The first solstice is the northern course (uttarāyaṇa), beginning with Capricorn and the month of Māgha; that very same solstice revolves through the six joint-wheels of the right and left arms.

Likewise, in the *kriyācakra*, within the thirty finger-joint wheels (*parvasandhi*) consisting of six channels each, the consonants beginning with *ka*—distinguished by the six long vowels—move through the wheel of each individual finger-joint in the joints of the fingers of the right hand according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*). In the left [hand], the consonants beginning with *ha* (representing space, etc.)—distinguished by the vowels beginning with *a* (representing space, etc.)—move according to the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*). Thus, the southern course [of the breath] occurs in the six joint-wheels of the feet known as the *karmacakra*, while [the same applies to] the finger-joints known as the *kriyācakra*.

In this context, during the month of Māgha at the Makara-saṃkrānti, the moon is to be understood according to the variation of lunar days (tithis), and the sun’s ascent according to the variation of the day of the week (vāra) of the saṃkrānti.
Where the sun increases, there is a waning of the moon; where the moon increases, there is a waning of the sun.

Thus, at the beginning of Makara and so forth, there is an increase of the sun. In Makara, within the thirty nāḍīs of the wheel at the joint of the right shoulder and arm, there are the thirty consonants beginning with *ka*, differentiated by long vowels.
The presiding deities (adhidevas) possess the nature of perception (*saṃjñā*), while [the letters] possess the nature of vital breath (*prāṇa*). Thus, in the first channel (*nāḍī*) there are *kkāḥ*;

likewise, in each of the three joints of all the fingers and toes, there are syllables in their respective order. For example: *kkāḥ*, *kklū*, *kkū*, *kkṝ*, *kkī*, *kkā*—these are in the six channels of the first [joint] of the action wheel (*kriyācakra*) at the joint below the thumb of the right hand. Similarly, *khāḥ*, *khkh*, *khkhū*, *khṝ*, *khkhī*, *khkhā*—these are in the six channels of the second [joint] of the action wheel at the joint below the index finger.

Likewise, *ggāḥ gglū ggū ggre ggaggī ggā* are in the six channels of the third [spoke] of the karma-cakra; *ṅaṅa* are in the six channels at the joint below the middle finger of the kriyā-cakra. Similarly, *dhghāḥ ghghlū ghghū ghṛ ghdhī ghghā* are in the six channels of the fourth [spoke] of the karma-cakra; [they are assigned] to the six channels at the joint below the ring finger of the kriyā-cakra.

Thus, in the fifth wheel of action (*karmacakra*), there are six channels in the sequence *ṅ-ṅāḥ-ṅ-ṅa-ṅa-ṅī-ṅṅā*; and in the wheel of activity (*kriyācakra*), there are six channels at the joint of the lower phalanx of the little finger.
In this manner, the Sun abandons each mandala, beginning with Earth, over the course of six days for each.
In thirty days, one abandons the five mandalas; thereafter, [the breath] enters the pitcher (kumbha) in the left channel (vāmanāḍī).
Therein is the sequence beginning with space (ākāśa);
and the *ka*-group [of consonants] is in the wheel of action (karmacakra), which is called the wheel of activity (kriyā).

Here, during the month of Phālguna or at the transit into Aquarius (kumbhasaṃkrānti), in the action wheel (karmacakra) at the joint of the left shoulder and arm, within the thirty channels (nāḍīs), there are the consonants beginning with *ṅa*, differentiated by the short vowels of space and so forth, corresponding to the mandalas of space and so on. For example: *ṅa ṅa ṅa ṅa ṅa ṅa*—these are in the six channels of the first group of six, characterized by the six mandalas of space and so forth, located at the joint of the lower phalanx of the left little finger in the action wheel.

Thus, *gha gha ghṛ ghughla ghaṃ*—these are in the six channels of the second wind-maṇḍala within the action-wheel (*kriyā-cakra*) at the joint below the ring finger in the activity-wheel (*karma-cakra*).
Likewise, *ga gi gṛ gu glū gaṃ*—these are in the six channels of the third fire-maṇḍala. Thus [is the sequence].

In the chapter on the "Great Chapter on the Signs of Death and Misfortune, the Severing of the Channels," these are in the six channels at the joint below the middle finger in the activity-wheel and the karma-wheel.

Thus, *kha*, *khi*, *khṛ*, *khla*, *khaṃ*—these [syllables] are in the six channels of the fourth water-maṇḍala, in the six channels at the joint below the ring finger in the action-wheel (*karmacakra*) and the activity-wheel (*kriyācakra*). Likewise, *ka*, *ki*, *kṛ*, *ku*, *kula*, *kaṃ*—these are in the six channels of the fifth earth-maṇḍala, in the six channels at the first joint below the thumb in the action-wheel and the activity-wheel of the six measures of the letter *ka*.

Thus, in one season, during the months of Capricorn (*makara*) and Aquarius (*kumbha*), the *mātrās* beginning with the sixteenth proceed by way of the distinction between withdrawal (*saṃhāra*) and emanation (*sṛṣṭi*) in the right and left [channels]. Then, from that group, he proceeds through the consonant groups together with their vowels according to the division of Pisces (*mīna*) and Aries (*meṣa*) at the joints of the right upper arm and forearm. In the wheel of action (*karmacakra*), he proceeds through the *ca*-group together with its vowels across thirty channels in the five mandalas of earth and the other elements, according to the division of the six days.
The withdrawal is as follows: *ccāḥ, cclū, ccū, ccū, ccī, ccā* on earth;
*chchā, chch, chchū, chchū, chchī, chchā* on water.
*Jjāḥ*, *jjlū*, *jjū*, *jj*, *jjī*, *jjā*—these are in fire.
*Jhjhāḥ*, *jhjhḷ*, *jhūjhū*, *jhajhajhajhī*, *jhjhā*—these are in air.
*Ññāḥ*, *ñ*, *ña*, *ñña*, *ññī*, *ñña*—these are in space.

The thirty measures are to be known as the thirty syllables beginning with *ca*, in the order of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), within the five joints—from the middle joint of the right thumb to the middle joint of the little finger—and within the six petals of the channels in both the wheel of karma and the wheel of action.

Thus, at the joint of the left upper arm and forearm in the *karmacakra*, there are thirty channels; and likewise, in the *kriyācakra*, there are thirty letters beginning with *tra* in the six sets of six channels at the five joints, starting from the middle phalanx of the little finger and ending at the middle phalanx of the thumb. They are as follows: *ña ñi ñū ña ñ* in the sphere of space (*ākāśamaṇḍala*); *jhajhi jha jhu jhū jhla jhaṃ* in wind (*vāyu*); *jaji jṛ ju jḷ jaṃ* in fire (*tejas*); *chachi chṛ chu chla chaṃ* in water (*toya*); and *cacici cu cla caṃ* in earth (*pṛthivī*).
Thus, as the spring season proceeds, the *ca*-group [of consonants] functions according to the division of the zodiac signs.

Then, at the joint of the upper arm of the right hand, in the *karmacakra* consisting of thirty channels, he traverses the *ṭa*-group by means of the division of the bull (*vṛṣabhabheda*) through the process of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), starting from the upper joint of the right thumb and proceeding through the five joints of six channels each. It is as follows: *ṭṭāḥ, ṭūḷa, ṭū, ṭṭu, ṭṭī, ṭṭā* in earth; *ṭhṭhāḥ, ṭhaṭha, ṭha, ṭhṭhī, ṭhṭhā* in water; *ḍḍāḥ, ḍḍḷ, ḍḍḍū, ḍḍḍa, ḍḍī, ḍḍā* in fire; *ḍhḍhāḥ, ḍhar̤ha, ḍha, ḍhḍhū, ḍhḍhī, ḍhḍhā* in air; *ṇṇāḥ, ṇṇa, ṇṇū, ṇṇū, ṇṇī, ṇṇā* in ether—thus by way of withdrawal.

Then, in the left arm at the joint of the upper arm, within the *karmacakra* (action wheel), there are thirty channels (*nāḍī*). In the *kriyācakra* (activity wheel), within the six channels at the joints of the upper phalanges and the lower phalanges of the left hand, starting from the little finger up to the thumb, there are the letters beginning with *ṇa*, according to the sequence of the spheres (*maṇḍala*) beginning with space. They are as follows: *ṇa, ṇi, ṇū, ṇu, ṇḷ, ṇaṃ* in space; *ḍha, ḍhi, ḍṛ, ḍḷ, ḍa, ḍaṃ* in wind; *ḍa, ḍi, ḍṛ, ḍu, ḍḷ, ḍaṃ* in fire; *ṭha, ṭhi, ṭha, ṭhu, ṭhḷ, ṭhaṃ* in water; and *ṭa, ṭi, ṭṛ, ṭu, ṭu, ṭaṃ* in earth. These move through the divisions of the zodiac signs Taurus and Gemini during the summer season.
Thus, during the northern course (uttarāyaṇa), the sun traverses one hundred and eighty syllables through the divisions of the zodiac signs over the duration of the solstice.

Afterwards, it moves upward by one [syllable] each day; subsequently, during the southern course (dakṣiṇāyana), death traverses the lunar apāna wind, while the sun moves upward and becomes diminished.

The moon waxes during the night; according to the principle that "death proceeds through the limbs of that which increases," the sun ascends from the joints of the fingers of the hands up to the head, as described in the *Vimalaprabhā* in the section on the internal [system], until it reaches the first channel of the joint of the right shoulder and arm.
Here, during the southern solstice (*dakṣiṇāyana*), the moon proceeds, entering the channels at the joint of the right hip and thigh in the wheel of karma (*karmacakra*).

From the lower joint of the right thumb to the lower joint of the little finger, by way of the process of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), thirty syllables of the *pa*-group move through the six channels at each of the five finger-joint articulations in the *kriyācakra*. By means of the Cancer division, [this constitutes] the lord of the three-year period; namely: *ppāḥ ppla ppū ppū ppī ppā* on earth; *phphāḥ phphla phphū phpha phphī phphā* on water; *bbāḥ bblū bbū bbū bbī bbā* on fire; *bbhāḥ bhbhla bhbhū bhū bhī bhbhā* on wind; *mmāḥ mm mmū mm mmī mmā* on space—thus, by way of the Cancer division.

Then, at the joint of the left hip and thigh, thirty syllables proceed in reverse order according to the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*) through the divisions of the mandalas beginning with space; namely: *ma mi mṛ mu mlṛ maṃ* in space; *bha bhi bhṛ bhu bhlṛ bhaṃ* in wind; *ba bi bṛ bu blū baṃ* in fire; *pha phi phṛ phu phlṛ phaṃ* in water; and *pa pi pṛ pu plū paṃ* in earth. Thus, the month of Bhādrapada proceeds by way of the division of the Leo transit (*siṃhasaṃkrānti*). In this manner, the moon traverses the rainy season (*vārṣya-ṛtu*), while the sun ascends (*utkramati*).

Then, at the joint of the right thigh and knee, in the *karmacakra* and *kriyācakra*, the *tavarga* (the dental class of consonants) moves through the six channels (*nāḍī*) located in the five joints, from the middle phalanx of the big toe to the middle phalanx of the little toe. From these, thirty syllables arise according to the divisions of the withdrawal of the zodiac signs (*rāśisaṃhāra*). They are as follows: *ttāḥ, tṛ, tū, ttu, ttī, ttā* in Earth; *ththāḥ, ththṛ, ththyū, ththyū, ththī, ththā* in Water; *ddāḥ, dṛ, ddī, ddā* in Fire; *dhdhāḥ, dhḷ, dhdhū, dhdhṛ, dhdhī, dhdhā* in Air; *nnāḥ, nn, ntu, nnu, nnī, nnā* in Space. Thus, the Moon moves according to the divisions of Virgo.

Then, at the junctions of the left thigh and knee—in the *karmacakra* or the *kriyācakra*—from the middle joint of the little toe of the left foot up to the big toe, across the five joints and six channels, [the vowels are placed] as follows: *na, ni, nṛ, nu, nḷ, naṃ* in space (*ākāśa*); likewise *dha, dhi, dhṛ, dhu, dhḷ, dhaṃ* in air (*vāyu*); similarly *da, di, dṛ, du, dḷ, daṃ* in fire (*tejas*); *tha, thi, thṛ, thu, thḷ, thaṃ* in water (*jala*); and *ta, ti, tṛ, tu, tlṛ, taṃ* in earth (*pṛthivī*). Thus, by way of the divisions of Libra, the Moon moves through the left side in the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*), while the Sun moves upward in the autumn season.

Then, on the right knee-joint, at the *karmacakra*, within the thirty channels (*nāḍī*), and on the five joints from the upper joint of the right thumb to the upper joint of the little finger, within the six sets of six channels, the Moon traverses the thirty letters of the *sa*-group together with their *mātrās* according to the order of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*) by means of the "scorpion" division (*vṛścikabheda*). On the right side, the Sun ascends; for example: *ssāḥ sslṛ ssū ssa ssī ssā* on the earth-mandala; *yyāḥ yyyyū yyū yyī yyā* on water; *ṣṣāḥ ṣṣlṛ ṣṣū ṣṣu ṣṣī ṣṣā* on fire; *śśāḥ śśla śśū śśū śśī śśā* on wind; and likewise *kkāḥ klṛ kū kṛ kī kā* on space—these are the thirty letters in the six channels by means of the "scorpion" division.

Then, in the action wheel (*karmacakra*) at the joint of the left knee, within the thirty channels, the moon traverses the thirty syllables in the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*) through the six channels in each of the five joints, from the upper phalanx of the little finger up to the upper phalanx of the thumb.

The Sun transcends the element of the shoulder in the left arm by way of the sign of Sagittarius (*dhanur-rāśi*). That is to say: *ka ki kṛ ku kla kaṃ* in space (*ākāśa*); likewise, *śa śi śṛ śu śla [śaṃ]* in wind (*vāyu*); *ṣa ṣi ṣṛ ṣu ṣla ṣaṃ* in fire (*tejas*); *yya yyi yyū yyu yyla yyaṃ* in water (*udaka*); and similarly, *sa si sṛ su sla saṃ* in earth (*pṛthivī*). Thus, these thirty syllables are by way of the division of Sagittarius. Therefore, beginning from the winter season (*śiśira-ṛtu*), there is an absence of the Moon's progression.

In the chapter on the Great Instruction on the Signs of Death, the Failure of the Channels, and the Cessation of Life: furthermore, there is an increase of the Sun at the beginning of Capricorn and so forth.

In the first year, Time proceeds together with the Sun and Moon according to the divisions of the *sattva* quality; then, in the second year, the thirty consonants beginning with *ka*—along with the vowels representing the increase of qualities (*guṇavṛddhi*) according to the divisions of *rajas*—are to be understood as before, within the thirty channels of the *karmacakra* and *kriyācakra*.

In the *makara* [sign], according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), it is as follows: *kkāḥ kkāl kkau kkār kkai kkā* on earth; likewise, *khkhāḥ khkhāl khkhī khkhār khkhai khkhā* on water; *ggāḥ ggāl ggauggār ggai ggā* on fire; *ghghāḥ ghghār ghghau ghghār ghye ghghā* on wind; and *ṅṅāḥ ṅṅāl ṅṅau ṅṅār ṅa ṅā* on the sphere of space. Thus, by means of the divisions of the *makara*, the Sun moves through the right arm as before; the Moon moves out from the right foot. Likewise, by means of the divisions of the *kumbha*, it moves through those [elements] accompanied by the qualities (*guṇa*) according to the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*) at the joint of the left arm. It is as follows: *ṅa ṅa ṅa ṅo ṅa ṅa* in space; *gha ghe ghar gho ghal ghaṃ* in wind; *ga ge gar go gal gaṃ* in fire; *kha khe khar kho khala khaṃ* in water; and *ka ke kar ko kala kaṃ* in earth. This is by means of the divisions of the *kumbha* on the left in the sequence of emanation. In this way, during the spring season, thirty letters of the *ca*-group [consonants] reside in the channel-joints of the right and left [limbs] respectively, according to the sequences of withdrawal and emanation; likewise, the letters of the *ṭa*-group [reside] in the summer season.

Thereupon the sun recedes and the moon advances. In Cancer and Leo, at the junction of the quarters, during thirty *nāḍīs*, the moon advances through the thirty syllables of the vowels and consonants as before, accompanied by the qualities of increase (*vṛddhi*) and multiplication (*guṇa*). In the rainy season, the moon advances through the syllables of the *pa*-group joined with the qualities of increase and multiplication; in autumn, the syllables of the *ta*-group; and in the cool season, the syllables of the *sa*-group, according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*) and emanation (*sṛṣṭi*).

Thus, in the second year, the moon and sun move sequentially through exactly three hundred and sixty measures; thereafter, in the third year, Time moves together with the sun from the consonant groups (ka-varga, etc. along with their vowels, according to the division of darkness.

Here, the vowel-substitutes (*yaṇādeśāḥ*) are stated: together with these, thirty syllables move within the sphere of *tamas* during the period of time, according to the divisions of withdrawal and emanation, as previously described, in the joints of the hands and feet, in the wheels of action (*karmacakra*) and the wheels of activity (*kriyācakra*). They are as follows: *kkhāḥ kklā kkvā kkā kkyā kkhā*—thus in earth, by way of the *makara* division; [*likewise*] *khkhhāḥ khlā khkhvā khkhā khkhyā khkhhā*—thus in water; likewise *gahāḥ galā gvā ggrā gayā rahā*—thus in fire; *ghghāḥ ghghlā ghghvā ghghrā ghyā ghghhā*—thus in air; *ṅhāḥ ṅlā ṅvā ṅkā ṅayāṅaṅahā*—thus in ether.
Thus the sun moves through the right side, and then through the left in the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*).
*Haṃ haya ṅ ṅva ṅlaṅahaṃ*—this is in space (*ākāśa*).
*Ghha ghya ghra ghva ghla ghhaṃ*—this is in wind (*vāyu*).
Gha, gya, gragva, gla, gre— these are in fire.
Khha, khya, khra, khva, khla, khhaṃ— these are in water.

Kha, Kya, Kra, Kva, Kla, Khūṃ—thus on the earth [plane]; likewise, during the winter season, the Sun moves through thirty mātrās in the left [nostril] by way of emanation. Similarly, in spring, the *ca*-group [is traversed], and in summer, the *ṭa*-group.
Then the Sun moves out from the six joints;
the Moon moves into the joint of the feet, and the *pavarga* [consonants] proceed as before, O Vārṣṇeya.
In autumn the *tavarga* [emerges], and in winter the *savarga*, according to the distinction of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*) and the distinction of emanation (*sṛṣṭi*).
Thus, in the third year as well, the Sun traverses three hundred and sixty measures (*mātrā*) in sequence.

Since there is indeed a deviation in the rainfall, therefore the decrease of those two [the sun and moon] should be understood as occurring over one thousand and eighty days; this is the rule that the cessation of the breath-nadīs (*nāḍī*) of the consonants occurs over three years.

Then, when the year has been cut off, within the fortnight, by the nature of the vowels—short, long, and protracted—and by the power of the vowel-days, which correspond to forty-five days, there is the ascent of death: by the division of the sun for the sun, and by the division of the moon for the moon.
